guide.title: Pediatric Assessment & Emergencies
guide.lead: Children compensate well, then crash. Most pediatric arrests start as a breathing problem or shock, so spot distress early from the doorway, treat it calmly with the parent close by, and use length-based doses.

sections.title: What the triangle tells you
rows: Appearance abnormal, breathing hard or too slow
Brain or metabolic problem: check glucose

sections.title: Normal vital signs (awake)
rows: Below 70 + (2 × age) to 10 years; then below 90 mmHg
notes: Tachycardia comes first; low blood pressure is a late sign.
Use a length-based tape (up to about 36 kg) for weight, doses and equipment.

sections.title: Stridor: croup or epiglottitis?
rows: Keep calm on the parent's lap; nebulized epinephrine for stridor at rest; dexamethasone
Don't look in the throat or lay the child down; oxygen as tolerated; go with pre-alert

rows.note: Or 4–8 puffs with a spacer; repeat as needed
With albuterol for moderate or severe attacks
Maximum 16 mg; oral, IM or IV

sections.title: Choking
sections.question: Coughing forcefully, crying or speaking?
sections.yes: Mild obstruction: let them cough, keep things calm, transport and watch for change.
sections.no: Severe: over 1 year, abdominal thrusts; under 1 year, 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts. Unresponsive: start CPR.

steps.title: Recognise
steps.text: Fast heart rate, capillary refill over 2 seconds, cold hands, sunken eyes or fontanelle, lethargy, few wet nappies.

steps.title: Fluids
steps.text: Isotonic bolus, reassess after each: lungs, liver, perfusion.

doses.note: 10 mL/kg if heart disease is possible

steps.title: Glucose
steps.text: Check it in every sick child.

sections.title: Also common
items: Febrile seizure: 6 months to 5 years, usually short. Treat any seizure lasting 5 minutes or more; look for meningitis.
Bronchiolitis: under 2 years. Suction the nose, oxygen if SpO₂ is below 90%; albuterol isn't routine.
BRUE: an infant under 1 year briefly stopped breathing or changed colour or tone, and is now well. Transport for assessment.
SVT: heart rate 220/min or more in infants, 180/min or more in children, no variability.

rows.note: 100–120/min. Infant about 4 cm deep (two thumbs encircling or heel of one hand); child about 5 cm
Later shocks up to 10 J/kg or the adult dose

items.label: SVT
items.sub: Infant: narrow, regular, 220/min or more. Vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine.

items.label: Bradycardia
items.sub: Below 60 with poor perfusion despite oxygen and ventilation: start CPR.

quiz.q: 3-year-old: barking cough, stridor only when crying, hoarse, worse at night, playing on the parent's lap. Most likely?
options: Croup: keep calm, position of comfort, transport
quiz.explanation: A playful, non-toxic child with a barking cough is croup.

quiz.q: 5-year-old: drooling, muffled voice, sitting forward with the mouth open, high fever since 4 hours ago. Best action?
options: Don't examine the throat; keep upright, oxygen as tolerated, rapid transport with pre-alert
Look in the throat with a tongue depressor
quiz.explanation: Epiglottitis: upsetting the child can cause complete obstruction.

quiz.q: 2-year-old with retractions, flaring, head bobbing, grunting, now pale and lethargic. PAT impression?
quiz.explanation: Abnormal appearance plus abnormal work of breathing means failure.

quiz.q: 6-month-old after 2 days of vomiting and diarrhoea: lethargic, sunken fontanelle, capillary refill 4 seconds, HR 180. Fluids?
options: IV/IO isotonic bolus 10–20 mL/kg, reassess, rapid transport
No fluids: these are normal infant findings
quiz.explanation: Shock: don't wait for low blood pressure, which comes late.

quiz.q: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle is done:
options: From the doorway, hands-off, in seconds
quiz.explanation: Appearance, work of breathing, circulation to skin.

quiz.q: A 4-year-old is hypotensive below a systolic of:
quiz.explanation: For ages 1–10 years: below 70 + (2 × age in years).

quiz.q: A 7-month-old is choking and can't cry. Do:
Infant, HR 240, narrow regular complexes, poor feeding, perfusion OK. Treatment?
options: Vagal manoeuvre (ice to the face), then adenosine 0.1 mg/kg
quiz.explanation: SVT in infants is 220/min or more; unstable → synchronized cardioversion.

quiz.q: 18-month-old, fever, 2-minute generalized seizure, now waking up. Most likely?
options: Febrile seizure: cool environment, check glucose, transport and look for infection
quiz.explanation: Treat a seizure lasting 5 minutes or more.

quiz.q: Infant with bronchiolitis, SpO₂ 92%, nose blocked. Most useful?

options: Two thumbs encircling the chest, or the heel of one hand
quiz.explanation: The two-finger technique is no longer recommended.

flashcards.question: Pediatric Assessment Triangle
flashcards.answer: Hands-off, from the doorway: Appearance (TICLS: tone, interactiveness, consolability, look, speech/cry), Work of breathing, Circulation to skin.

flashcards.question: Child airway differences
flashcards.answer: Large head and occiput (pad under the shoulders), large tongue, small narrow airway, floppy epiglottis, higher larynx. Small swelling causes big obstruction.

flashcards.question: Commonest cause of cardiac arrest in children
flashcards.answer: Respiratory failure or shock, not a primary heart problem. Recognise and treat distress early.

flashcards.question: Croup vs epiglottitis
flashcards.answer: Croup: days, barking cough, stridor, hoarse. Epiglottitis: hours, high fever, drooling, tripod, muffled voice, no cough – don't look in the throat.

flashcards.question: Severe dehydration
flashcards.answer: Lethargy, sunken eyes and fontanelle, dry mouth, capillary refill over 2 seconds, fast heart rate, few wet nappies. Low BP is late.

flashcards.question: Length-based tape
flashcards.answer: Estimates weight (up to about 36 kg) and gives doses and equipment sizes. Children are not small adults.

flashcards.question: BRUE
flashcards.answer: Brief resolved unexplained event: an infant under 1 year briefly stopped breathing or changed colour or tone, now well. Take a careful history and transport.

flashcards.question: Normal heart rates (awake)
flashcards.answer: Newborn 100–205; infant 100–180; toddler 98–140; preschool 80–120; school age 75–118; adolescent 60–100.

critical.scenario: 2-year-old, 2 days of cold symptoms, now wheezing with retractions and nasal flaring. Pink, fussy but consolable on the mother's lap; worse when crying. Known asthma, inhaler ran out. HR 152, RR 44, SpO₂ 92%.
critical.question: PAT impression and plan?

options.t: Respiratory distress: keep with the parent, albuterol by nebulizer or spacer, blow-by oxygen if tolerated, upright, reassess, transport

options.f: Crying worsens the wheeze; treat first.

critical.explanation: Avoid upsetting procedures until breathing improves.
critical.kpi: Uses the PAT to classify respiratory distress and treats asthma appropriately

critical.scenario: 4-year-old choking on a grape: coughing forcefully, making sounds, face red. Bystanders shout to do the Heimlich.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Mild obstruction: encourage coughing, calm the scene, watch closely, ready to act if the cough fails; transport

options.f: Not while the cough is effective.

critical.explanation: If the cough becomes silent or weak: abdominal thrusts (over 1 year).
critical.kpi: Distinguishes partial from complete airway obstruction

critical.scenario: 8-month-old found blue and not breathing in a cot 5 minutes ago after a nap face-down on a soft pillow. Limp, apnoeic, no pulse, cool skin; no rigor or lividity.
critical.question: Priorities?

options.t: Start CPR (two thumbs encircling or heel of one hand, 15:2), bag-mask with oxygen, IO, epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg, transport; support the family and note the scene

options.f: No obvious signs of death; resuscitate.

options.t: Two-finger compressions at 30:2 with two rescuers
options.f: Two rescuers use 15:2; two fingers is no longer recommended.

options.t: Wait for police before touching the baby

critical.explanation: Most pediatric arrests are asystole or PEA. Leave the bedding; record how and where the baby was found.
critical.kpi: Initiates pediatric resuscitation and preserves scene information in SUID
